Only the rows that were misclassified

q: In addition to bagging, random forests also:
options: Consider a random subset of features at each split
Prune each tree to one level

q: For large n, the share of rows NOT in a given bootstrap sample approaches:

The training rows the tree saw

q: A random forest mainly reduces a single tree's:
options: Bias, to zero in every case

q: Adding more trees to a forest generally:
options: Levels off in accuracy without much overfitting, at a cost in time

options: Harder to read and slower to run
Less accurate in nearly all cases
